sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Off-Price Wholesale Liquidation of Branded Overstock Apparel

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley N° 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework); Ley N° 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations); Ley N° 129 de 18 de diciembre de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); implementing Resoluciones and regulations of the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) and the Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministry of Economy and Finance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Panamanian resident agent and foundation council
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary or company registry in the founder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Apostille jurisdictions, consular legalization by the Panama consulate with jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Founder's and ultimate beneficial owner's certified passport copies and proof of address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or relevant national identification authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, together with Spanish/English notarized translation if required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Good Standing, and incumbent director/officer proof for any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the corporate founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; translation into Spanish must accompany the filing

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Statement and AML risk declaration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian legal counsel / resident agent in accordance with Law 23 of 2015 and Law 129 of 2020
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed before the Panamanian notary as part of the foundation charter dossier

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of the founder, foundation council members, protector, and ultimate beneficial owners against OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's domestic list circulated by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, family members, and close associates under Law 23 of 2015 and FATF Recommendation 12. The resident agent must document all screening results and maintain AML/CFT records for at least five years after termination of the foundation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá Online Services Portal – Dirección Nacional de Registro y Fundaciones de Interés Privado
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Spanish is the official language; all statutory names accepted for registration must use the Latin alphabet and be reproducible in Spanish script. A foundation name must include an identifying word such as 'Fundación' or 'Foundation'. If a foreign-language name is used, the registered agent must provide a Spanish transliteration or descriptive translation. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity in the Registro Público de Panamá; accent marks and diacritical marks are generally normalized for electronic search purposes.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Bank / Financiera – requires prior banking license and Superintendencia de Bancos approval
Seguros / Reaseguros / Insurance – requires prior insurance regulatory authorization
Fideicomiso / Trust / Fiduciaria – requires trust-license authorization in Panama
Gobierno / Autoridad / Ministerio / Público – suggests sovereign or governmental sponsorship and requires ministerial authorization
Cámara / Colegio / Cruz Roja / Rotary / Caja de Ahorros – protected institutional identifiers requiring prior consent or statutory prohibition
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days. An extension may be sought by re-filing the availability request and paying the corresponding registry tariff before the initial window lapses. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant or registered agent may file a recurso de reconsideración with the Registro Público de Panamá within five business days of notification; if denied, a further recurso de apelación may be filed with the Director General of the Registro Público. Final judicial review is available before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. All filings must be made through the official registry portal with evidence of fee payment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Private Interest Foundation must continuously maintain a resident agent and a registered office in Panama at the physical office of that resident agent. A virtual-only registered office is not permissible for statutory service of process. Remote management by the founder and foundation council is permitted, but the resident agent must keep the statutory records, client due diligence file, UBO declarations, and notice-of-service capability in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk, estimated at less than 5 percent annual probability for an off-price wholesale apparel liquidation foundation classified as standard risk. Unannounced physical inspections may occur under the risk-based supervision of the UAF and Registro Público and are directed primarily at the resident agent's registered office, foundation charter, UBO records, and AML/CFT documentation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended by Ley No. 12 de 2016 and Ley No. 15 de 17 de mayo de 2024; Articles 4 (charter contents), 8 (registration), 19 (minimum endowment), 21-23 (Foundation Council) and 24 (Resident Agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección General de Registro, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Fundación (Foundation Charter), executed as a notarized private instrument or public deed (escritura pública) by the founder and Resident Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Mandatory minimum endowment of US$10,000.00 (B/.10,000.00) per Article 19 of Law 25 of 1995; capital may consist of tangible or intangible assets, must be expressly declared in the Acta de Fundación, and must be accepted by the Foundation Council at its first meeting. No statutory escrow account is required; the declared endowment determines the Public Registry tariff and ISAN stamp tax.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST MEETING OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL — RESOLUTION No. 1. At Panama City on this day, the undersigned founders and members of the Foundation Council of PA_PIF, seated in inaugural session, unanimously RESOLVE: First, the Foundation Charter deposited with the Public Registry of Panama is ratified and approved in entirety. Second, the initial endowment of US$10,000.00 is declared subscribed and is accepted by the Council as satisfying Article 19 of Law 25 of 1995. Third, the Registered Office at [Panama City] is adopted as the foundation's seat. Fourth, [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed President, Secretary and Treasurer of the Council, jointly and severally empowered. Fifth, the Resident Agent is ratified in office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Resident Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certificado de Búsqueda office (via licensed Resident Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Panamanian attorney licensed to act as Resident Agent; the agent files a name search (certificado de búsqueda) through the Public Registry's Sede Electrónica to confirm the proposed foundation name is distinguishable from existing registered entities. Secure written acceptance of the agency mandate and registered-office agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a conflictive or identical name is found, the Resident Agent immediately files substitute names; third-party opposition is resolved by the Director of the Public Registry and may be cured by consent or name amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Legalization of the Acta de Fundación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (with Resident Agent certification)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter covering the name, object, endowment, Foundation Council provisions, beneficiary and protector (if any) clauses, and Resident Agent clause; execute before a Panamanian Notary Public or as a private instrument countersigned by the Resident Agent; pay applicable ISAN stamp tax and notarial fees.
required_dossiers: Notarized passport copies of founder and council members
Resident Agent letter of acceptance and licensed attorney credential
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial observations are cured by re-execution of the instrument; ISAN stamp deficiencies are settled by supplementary tax payment and re-presentation to the Notary or the Resident Agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment and Registration at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original Acta de Fundación together with the search certificate and fee voucher to the Private Interest Foundations Section; pay the approximate B/.250.00 registration tariff at the Registry cashier; obtain the filed-entry receipt (comprobante) and await substantive review and registration by the examining officer.
required_dossiers: Copy of Resident Agent professional license (carné)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect notice (razón de defecto) is issued, the Resident Agent files corrective documents within ten working days; failure to cure results in rejection, after which full re-submission with new fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certified Registration Certificate (Copia Registrada)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Archivo General y Sección de Certificaciones
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the entry is perfected, request an official certified copy (Copia Registrada / Certificación de Fundación) evidencing legal existence and the foundation's registration number; verify Ficha data against the Acta de Fundación for accuracy.
required_dossiers: Written request from the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains registry or transcription errors, file a rectification petition (aclaración) before the Registrar; corrected certificate is reissued after approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Foundation Council Meeting, Reglamento, and Opening of Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Foundation Council (internal corporate governance; no State filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the Foundation Council adopting Resolution No. 1; approve the internal Reglamento (by-laws); open the minute book, council-member register, and accounting records; have the President and Secretary sign the first minutes.
required_dossiers: Blank corporate books (minutes and member register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inconsistent minutes are corrected by a supplementary council resolution; if financial institutions request apostilled or notarized extracts, the Resident Agent prepares certified copies without re-registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Municipal Registration (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Alcaldía / Municipio del domicilio
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation's taxpayer identification number (RUC/NIT) with DGI via Sede Electrónica; apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación for wholesale trading premises; confirm territorial treatment of off-price garment sales (non-Panamanian buyers are generally outside Panamanian income tax). Open a corporate bank account only after RUC is issued.
required_dossiers: Lease or title proof of commercial premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries documentation, amend and resubmit electronically; municipal administrative fines for late Aviso de Operación are paid and the permit is re-filed; appeals follow Ley 38 de 2000 administrative procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Empresas (no industrial manufacturing license applies to ISIC 4641 wholesale textile liquidation; only the municipal Aviso de Operación and DGI RUC are mandated for the trading activity).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) — municipal commercial license for wholesale apparel trading and warehousing premises issued by the local Alcaldía.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I — Registration / Exempt from Full EIA Report (wholesale trading and bonded storage of finished garments generates no significant environmental impact and is outside Categories II and III of the EIA regulation; a Category I registration may be required only if the warehouse exceeds local thresholds or carries out washing, dyeing, or printing, which are excluded from this scope).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater and no VOC-generating operations; sanitary discharges must comply with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 8 de 2019 (wastewater discharge parameters); solid waste handling per Ley 6 de 2018 (Panama's General Waste Law); fire protection and storage density per NFPA 13 and NFPA 25 standards with textile inventory kept in segregated, sprinkler-protected racks.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety inspection and annual certification for warehouse premises; structural load inspection of racking systems; workplace hygiene and occupational health registration with Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); import-export of finished garments requires no sectoral license but customs clearance through SENACOM (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) of the Republic of Panama; online portal: Sede Electrónica (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa). Complementary customs authority for export controls: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the VUPEA single window (https://www.ana.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Constitute the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995 (as amended) through a licensed Panamanian resident agent and record the foundation charter in the Registro Público de Panamá. Step 2 — Obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente / TIN) at the DGI through Sede Electrónica or in person: submit the foundation deed, Public Registry inscription certificate, identification of founder and members of the Foundation Council, and notarized appointment of a fiscal representative (representante legal) with a local address; the RUC is pre-assigned and the definitive taxpayer certificate is issued electronically. Step 3 — Activate the ITBMS (VAT) registration in the RUC and enroll in the SFE electronic-invoicing platform. Step 4 — Settle the flat annual foundation tax of PAB/USD 300 (due by 30 June of each year) through DGI treasury collection channels; the DGI payment receipt (paz y salvo) is a prerequisite for subsequent administrative acts. Step 5 — A municipal Aviso de Operación or patent fee is triggered only if the PIF maintains a physical commercial establishment in Panama; no sector-specific license is required for off-price apparel wholesale liquidation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — Panama exempts foreign-source income; a PIF is a separate legal person which, for domestic tax purposes, is subject to entity-level Corporate Income Tax (ISR) at the standard 25% rate solely on net Panama-source income, plus a 10% dividend or branch remittance tax where profits are distributed to non-resident beneficiaries. All income derived from sources outside Panama, including offshore off-price trading margins on finished garments, foreign dividends, bank interest, and capital gains realized abroad, falls outside the Panamanian tax jurisdiction provided the purchase order, delivery, risk of loss, and payment occur outside Panama and the merchandise never enters Panamanian customs territory. The PIF also bears the flat annual foundation tax of PAB/USD 300 under Law 25 of 1995.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no domestic check-the-box election and no hybrid-mismatch-specific election, although Panama ratified the OECD Multilateral Instrument (effective 2020). Available statutory elections and administrative options: (i) election of the small-taxpayer simplified regime ('pequeño contribuyente') where authorized by DGI for low-income taxpayers, replacing standard monthly ITBMS filings with fixed quotas; (ii) election of the fiscal-year accounting period with prior DGI notification (calendar year remains the default); (iii) exporter-status election enabling ITBMS credit refund applications; (iv) optional re-domiciliation of the PIF under Law 25 to change governing law and administrative seat; and (v) for foreign federal tax purposes only (e.g., the United States), the PIF may be eligible for a US check-the-box classification, while under Panamanian domestic law it remains an entity-level taxpayer and no domestic pass-through election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama national VAT and general sales-and-use tax), governed by Law 15 of 1995 as amended and its implementing regulations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None under the standard regime — any enterprise (including a PIF) performing taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable act. A simplified small-taxpayer quota regime applies to economically small taxpayers with gross annual income at or below PAB/USD 60,000, subject to DGI qualification; wholesale off-price garment liquidation entities are normally captured by the standard monthly ITBMS regime at the 7% rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica de Panamá) applies to all active taxpayers through the DGI SFE platform under a phased incorporation calendar. Sales invoices, credit notes, and debit notes must be generated in the DGI-approved XML/PDF format, transmitted through the SFE free web portal or via automated API/SFTP integration for high-volume issuers, and validated by DGI real-time fiscal clearance; each accepted invoice carries a digitally stamped QR/verification code. Any invoice issued outside the SFE without DGI authorization is invalid for ITBMS input-credit and export-refund purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when the goods are physically removed from Panamanian customs territory, the PIF is the exporter of record on the customs declaration, and legal title and risk pass to a non-resident buyer. Services qualify for 0% when rendered to a non-resident recipient, paid from outside Panama, and effectively consumed or economically used outside Panama. For off-price apparel liquidation: pure offshore drop-ship trades with no entry into Panama generate foreign-source income outside the scope of ITBMS altogether; if goods are imported into Panama and subsequently re-exported, the re-export is zero-rated and the ITBMS paid at importation (input credit) may be offset or reclaimed from DGI as an exporter credit refund (solicitud de devolución de saldo a favor), subject to full documentary substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) processed through ANA VUPEA/SISCOA single window and electronically linked to DGI
Original or electronic Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued to the foreign importer evidencing physical exit of the finished-garment shipment
Commercial invoice, packing list, purchase order, or letter of credit mirroring the exact goods, quantities, prices, and zero-rated sale terms
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice (SWIFT/ACH statement) showing receipt of proceeds from the foreign buyer into a Panamanian or foreign bank account
Evidence of the input ITBMS credit underlying the refund claim (import entries, customs duty and ITBMS payment receipts, purchase invoices of the overstock inventory)
Certificate of origin or free-sale documentation where the destination jurisdiction requires it for apparel imports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI risk-based audits reconcile customs export declarations, vessel and master data, and banking inflows; exporters failing to prove physical exit and receipt of foreign exchange within the 180-day evidentiary benchmark face retroactive ITBMS at 7% on the gross export value, monthly surcharge of 1.5% on the unpaid tax, and fines up to 100% of the deficiency. Fabricated or dual-use export documentation triggers criminal tax fraud (defraudación tributaria) under Law 70 of 2019 with imprisonment of three to five years, cumulative ANA customs penalties, money-laundering reporting consequences under Panamanian AML rules in cases of false remittances, and clawback of refunds with statutory interest within the applicable DGI assessment limitation period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama does not operate a classical central bank. Banking and payment-system supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The Banco Nacional de Panamá (state-owned) serves as fiscal agent of the Republic and clearing agent for public-sector funds, while the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees fiscal and financial policy. The United States dollar is de facto legal tender; the Balboa is a nominal coin-only unit at a fixed 1:1 parity with the USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The regime is one of complete, unrestricted convertibility. There are no exchange-control laws, no capital-account barriers, no prior-approval requirements for foreign investment, and no restrictions on profit or capital repatriation. The Balboa does not float independently and simply mirrors the USD. Consequently, a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) conducting off-price apparel liquidation can move funds freely in USD to Latin America, Asia, and Europe. The only frictions are bank-commission and compliance costs at transaction level, not regulatory convertibility limits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export-proceeds surrender requirement. A PIF may retain 100% of export sale proceeds in USD in any onshore or offshore account, and may settle supplier invoices directly from an overseas USD or multi-currency account. Holding export proceeds offshore triggers no penalty; the only obligations are accurate accounting under Panama's territorial taxation rules and full bank disclosure sufficient for SWIFT and OFAC name-screening protocols.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Treasury Account
Operational Account with segregated Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Operational Account and Documentary LC Facility Account
Operational Account with online treasury module
Operational Account and Multi-Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for USD settlement through SBP-licensed digital banks; Low for pure offshore non-licensed EMIs. Panama's FinTech Hub regulatory sandbox, administered by SBP under the Panamanian FinTech law framework, permits supervised digital banks and electronic-money institutions to be licensed. An overseas EMI (e.g., an FCA-licensed UK EMI or a US MSB) cannot independently open a domestic clearing account at a Panamanian bank without SBP licensing; it may, however, function as a front-end payment-instruction platform routing into a Panamanian bank-owned IBAN. Legal constraint: operating an unlicensed payment service or holding client funds in USD within Panama territory is prohibited; a PIF may use licensed foreign EMIs only for non-resident treasury operations, not for domestic payroll or clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the ultimate beneficial owner is the general rule for tier-1 Panamanian banks during initial underwriting interviews. The PIF's resident agent, legal counsel, and notarized/apostilled foundation resolutions do not waive beneficial-owner verification. SBP remote customer-due-diligence rules permit assisted video interviews and digital KYC where the bank operates an approved secure electronic verification platform; Banco General and Multibank accept remote onboarding for low-risk corporate structures only with a prior banker introduction. Practical mandate: most tier-1 banks require either (i) personal appearance at headquarters by the beneficial owner, or (ii) remote visual verification by video call with an assigned bank officer, combined with apostilled statutory documents, certified passport copies, and the original-signature (notarized) of each appointed director on account-opening forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF beneficial-ownership opacity under Panama's Registered Beneficial Owners framework
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized Foundation Charter (Estatutos); Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) filing certificate issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); certified Directors' Resolution authorizing account opening; full ownership/control chart; passport copies and proof of residential address for each ultimate beneficial owner; signed PEP self-certification form; executed waiver of foundation secrecy clause specifically authorizing bank disclosure to SBP and correspondent banks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Branded overstock provenance and counterfeit anti-piracy concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original clearance and liquidation contracts executed directly with brand owners or authorized licensed distributors; supplier invoices and packing lists; customs declarations evidencing lawful import/export; authenticity or quality certificates issued by the brand; release-of-lien or security-interest documentation when inventory was previously collateralized; and a lot-level traceability ledger covering purchase, warehousing, and resale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border wires inconsistent with declared revenue profile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or independent-reviewed financial statements of the foundation; twelve-month cash-flow forecast and working-capital model; supplier distribution list with country and invoice frequency; invoice-level transaction log showing average ticket size; and a sworn source-of-funds declaration linking each capital injection to the underlying liquidation agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth for injected capital from non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the originator's primary bank; the capital-contribution agreements or shareholder loan agreements; sworn declaration of funds (Declaración Jurada de Origen de Fondos); up-to-date tax residence certificate for each beneficial owner; and, where applicable, audited financial statements or sale-and-purchase contracts evidencing the historical wealth creation of the contributor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: (1) The originator shareholder or capital contributor sends USD via SWIFT MT103 to the PIF's account at Banco General, Banistmo, or Multibank, with the correspondent leg settled through the bank's US partner via Fedwire or CHIPS. (2) Recommended wire narrative: 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — CAPITALIZATION RESOLUTION NO. [X]' together with the Foundation's RUC (tax ID) number. The bank requires the capitalization minutes and confirmation that the beneficiary account passes OFAC name-screening; receipt of sanctioned-related funds is prohibited and mandates immediate freeze. (3) For amounts above USD 100,000, banks pre-clear the transaction with the internal anti-money-laundering officer, obtaining the equity-injection resolution, the Foundation Charter, and a source-of-funds declaration. (4) Panama operates no separate FDI declaration system; foreign direct investment is registered for statistical purposes only, and the wire itself is the recognized capital-injection record for territorial-tax exemption purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 open-account wire transfers for routine supplier payments below USD 500,000 per invoice, used for recurring purchases of overstock garments from Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Turkey; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary sight or usance LCs) issued by a tier-1 Panamanian bank for high-value branded-liquidation contracts, with transferable and confirmed LC structures allowing 90–120 day tenors and payment upon presentation of compliant shipping documents; (iii) domestic USD clearing through Panama's ACH/Cámara de Compensación for local commission and logistics payables; and (iv) ACH Direct merchant settlement rails for e-commerce liquidation receivables. SWIFT MT103 remains the statutory-standard cross-border trade disbursement method, with 2–3 business-day execution through the bank's US correspondent network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (USD/CNY, USD/EUR, USD/GBP) executed with SBP-licensed banks or non-resident investment-grade counterparties to fix procurement costs of branded overstock sourced from China, Europe, and Turkey.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-fully-convertible currencies (CNY, INR, TRY), permissible for offshore USD settlement because Panama maintains no exchange-control regime requiring physical delivery.
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/EUR and USD/CNY) to align funding and treasury liquidity where the PIF receives euro or renminbi liquidation proceeds and requires USD operating cash.

FX Options and zero-cost collars (USD/CNH, USD/EUR) to protect minimum conversion rates on HK/Asian resale receipts while preserving upside, subject to internal treasury policy approval and recorded board minutes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Tax remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; remitted through the Panama Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment triggers USD 50 penalty plus 10% annual interest; after 30 days of non-payment, the foundation cannot obtain a certificate of good standing; continued default for 3 consecutive years may lead to administrative strike-off by the Public Registry upon DGI certification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation to the Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Resident Agent, acting under AML Law 23 of 2015; no public registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the foundation’s anniversary date and within 15 days of any change in the beneficial ownership or beneficiary structure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current UBO records is an AML compliance breach; fines under Law 23 of 2015 may be imposed and repeated non-compliance can result in entity cancellation by court order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit applies to Panama Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995; an audit is required only if the Foundation Charter or the Foundation Council expressly mandates it, regardless of asset or revenue thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting framework is imposed. Where books are prepared, they are generally kept under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or Panama GAAP; records may be maintained in any currency and language.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no public UBO filing for Private Interest Foundations. The Resident Agent must obtain an annual written confirmation from the Foundation Council identifying current beneficiaries and recording any transfers of beneficial interests; mid-year changes must be reported within 15 days. This is an AML due-diligence requirement under Law 23 of 2015, not a public registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners maintained by the Resident Agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350–1,200 per year depending on the corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 – audit not legally required; voluntary certified audit typically USD 1,500–5,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: foreign-source income is wholly exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax. For Panamanian-source net taxable income up to USD 1.5 million, the statutory rate is reduced to 15%; the 25% headline rate applies only to the excess above USD 1.5 million. A 5% dividend tax credit is available when the underlying corporate income tax has already been paid; special economic zones (e.g., City of Knowledge, Panama Pacifico, Colon Free Zone) may grant 100% income tax exemptions for qualifying operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1933 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta – Personas Jurídicas) filed electronically through the DGI e-Tax portal 'SITIA' (Sistema de Información Tributaria Integrado).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly provisional advance payments (due 10 April, 10 July, 10 October, and 10 December).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed on or before 15 April following the close of the fiscal year (calendar year for most entities); a one-month automatic extension to 15 May applies upon submission of a request through SITIA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year identification (start and end dates)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact fiscal period; for a PIF owned by non-residents, use the calendar year unless another fiscal year has been approved by the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) and legal identification of the entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the foundation's RUC and importer/exporter registration number; foreign owner ID is declared in the beneficial ownership schedule, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue derived from Panamanian source commercial activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only revenue from the sale of goods delivered, used, or originating in Panama is taxable; income from offshore liquidation sales (e.g., goods shipped directly from a warehouse in the Colon Free Zone to foreign buyers) must be identified as foreign-source and excluded from taxable gross revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: cost of goods sold, operating expenses, and permitted accruals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach supporting transfer pricing documentation for intercompany purchases and commissions; expenses allocated to foreign-source income are non-allocable and must be excluded from the Panamanian tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (assessable base after statutory adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure foreign-source exempt income and related expenses are reconciled in the attached breakdown; no tax is payable on that component.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed at 25% (or 15% on the first USD 1.5 million of taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are not subject to any additional tax at entity level beyond the corporate income tax; the final tax is the same for local and foreign owners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax payments made during the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all quarterly provisional payments made on behalf of the PIF; missing or late advances attract surcharges and are credited against the final liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance due or carry-forward credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the balance is due, payment must be made on or before the filing deadline; foreign owners may settle through a local corporate bank account in USD, but must not pay in-kind or via third-party offsets.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certificate of compliance: signature of the legal representative and registered accountant (Revisor Fiscal / Contador Público Autorizado)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Panamanian registered agent (or an appointed attorney-in-fact) must certify the return; foreign owners cannot sign unless they hold a valid Panama visa and tax ID.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return incurs a monthly fine of 1% of the tax due (capped at 25% of the tax, with a minimum of USD 100), plus compound interest at 10% per annum. Failure to file a valid return within two months triggers automatic assessment by the DGI based on estimated income. Additionally, any underpayment detected on audit is subject to a 15%-25% accuracy penalty, and pervasive non-compliance may result in the suspension of the PIF's commercial registration, impediments to travel, and the prohibition of operations in Panama.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends paid from Panamanian-source profits. The rate is reduced to 0% on distributions of foreign-source profits (which are exempt at the corporate level) and may be effectively reduced to 5% when the distributing PIF has already paid corporate income tax at 25% on the underlying profits, because the corporate tax is creditable against the dividend withholding. Where the PIF is in the reduced 15% bracket for its first USD 1.5 million of taxable income, the dividend withholding rate on that portion is 10% with no corporate tax credit.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's tax treaties (with the Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Barbados, and Mexico) generally reduce dividend WHT to 5% or 10% and royalties to 5%. To apply treaty relief: (1) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority of the recipient; (2) complete the DGI's 'Certificado de Residencia Fiscal – Beneficiario Efectivo' form, including the beneficial ownership declaration; (3) submit the TRC, the form, and a copy of the applicable tax treaty to the DGI at least 15 days before the distribution/transfer; (4) obtain a written advance resolution of the DGI confirming the reduced rate; and (5) instruct the paying agent to withhold at the treaty rate only after the DGI-approved resolution is issued. The protocol applies to royalties, interest, dividends, and similar remittances to non-residents. If the DGI does not issue the resolution before the remittance date, the full statutory rate must be withheld and the excess may be reclaimed via a tax refund process (Form 2303).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory WHT of 15% for payments of trademarks, designs, patents, and 'know-how' to non-residents; treaty rate usually 5%. Interest: statutory WHT of 10% for non-resident lenders; treaty rate commonly 5%, and the Panama-Netherlands treaty grants a 0% rate on certain bank-held credits. No WHT applies to interest paid on deposits maintained in Panamanian banks by non-residents. Payments for technical assistance intercompany services are treated as royalties for WHT purposes if the principal value is in the transfer of IP or technical knowledge.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 1,000,000 in aggregate related-party transactions during the fiscal year. Annual simultaneous documentation (Local File) must be prepared and submitted to the DGI within 150 days after year-end; a Master File is additionally required when the MNE group exceeds USD 500 million in global consolidated revenue or the entity's related-party transactions exceed USD 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has no general statutory Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) comparable to the BVI/Cayman framework for pure commercial trading vehicles. However, the DGI applies the 'economic substance doctrine' as an anti-avoidance principle: for a PIF engaged in cross-border apparel liquidation, the following must be demonstrable to protect the territorial exemption and treaty benefits: (a) an adequate Panamanian office with independent management, (b) the foundation's bank account and accounting records maintained in Panama, (c) substantive business decisions made in Panama, and (d) real commercial activity with sufficient risk-bearing. Free-trade-zone licensees, reinsurance companies, and financial institutions are expressly subject to published ESR guidelines. Where a PIF has no substance beyond the registered agent, the tax authorities may reclassify foreign-source revenue as taxable Panamanian-source income and invalidate the economic benefit of the territorial exemption.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-reporting of Panamanian-source gross revenue, overstating deductible expenses, or concealing the origin of inventory (e.g., booking offshore shipments as local sales to extract amplified refunds).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of 100% to 500% of the omitted tax, plus default interest at the legal rate; disqualification from government contracts and the loss of the right to carry forward losses. Where the amount exceeds USD 250,000, the entity is permanently barred from operating as a foundation and its Panama commercial registration is cancelled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council and the registered manager become vicariously liable for restitution of the total evaded tax, may face a travel ban issued by the DGI in coordination with migration police, and can be imprisoned for up to 10 years under Panamanian Criminal Code Article 283. The DGI can pierce the corporate veil upon showing that the PIF is a mere instrumentality used to perpetrate fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Artificial Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a PIF with zero physical presence, no functional management, and no commercial activity other than passing invoices for third-party apparel transactions, thereby exploiting the territorial exemption and treaty benefits for offshore groups.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may disregard the PIF as a sham entity, treat its shareholders/founders as the direct taxpayers, and impose the full CIT liability at 25% plus surcharges on their behalf. A certificate of 'no substance' issued by the DGI triggers the loss of the entity's beneficial status, cancellation of the PIF registration under Law 25 of 1995, and disqualification of the resident agent. Administrative fines of USD 5,000 to USD 50,000 may be imposed for each fiscal year of sham operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the foundation council are jointly and severally liable for the reclassified tax liability. They are barred from serving as directors of any Panama-licensed entity for 5 years and may be subject to passport seizure and a prohibition on business travel to Panama while the assessment is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash settlement or high-volume wire transfers for overstock apparel without maintaining required AML registries; acting as an informal value transferor (i.e., laundering proceeds through the PIF bank account); or failing to report AML red flags to the UAF (Unidad de Análisis Financiero) despite having MSB obligations in the distribution chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Law 23 of 2015 carry fines from USD 10,000 up to USD 1,000,000 per incident, plus the freezing of bank account(s). Criminal charges for organized money laundering may result in imprisonment from 5 to 12 years, forfeiture of the foundation's assets, and dissolution of the entity. The PIF loses its benefit of confidentiality if used for criminal ends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly authorise a transaction that constitutes money laundering are individually subject to a prison term equal to the primary offender's sentence, a fine of USD 250,000, and asset seizure of personal property; they additionally face a 10-year travel ban from Panama and a prohibition on holding fiduciary licences in the Canal Zone.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany supply of branded garments at non-arm's-length prices to a Panama PIF that then re-invoices at full markup to the same group, artificially accumulating profits and claiming that the resulting trade is foreign-source and therefore tax-exempt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by the DGI to the arm's-length profit, application of a 20% accuracy penalty, plus interest at compound rates. If the adjustment results in tax larger than USD 300,000, the DGI may initiate criminal fraud proceedings. Loss of the territorial exemption for the manipulated transactions and retroactive assessment for the last 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation's legal representative who signs the inaccurate tax return is personally liable for the penalty equal to 25% of the entire adjusted tax liability, and if the mispricing exceeds USD 1 million, the representative is subject to imprisonment for up to 4 years and a civil restitution order in favour of the State. Travel restrictions may be applied pending the payment of the adjustment.
